```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
options(digits=2)
require(tidyverse)
require(tigerstats)
require(lubridate)
kRdata <- read.csv(file = 'kRdata.csv')
kRdata <- kRdata %>%
mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))
kData = kRdata
```
Data are from the Patient_Info dataset from South Korea 1 Jan to 1 May 2020. These data were retrieved from a downloadable zip file from kaggle.

Some of the data were uncoded for sex - sex must be just male or female.  77 of the data entries were coded sex as blank, so we omit these.  State of a patient must be died or alive - we adjust that as well.  This is done in the mutate function. 

Variables of interest: sex, result

Research Question: - Is dying independent of sex?

# Introduction
Based of the dataset from the Patient_Info dataset from South Korea, is death independent from sex concerning Covid-19? 

$H_0$: There is no relationship between Covid-19 deaths and the sex of the patient in South Korea from January to May of 2020. 

$H_A$: There is a relationship between Covid-19 deaths and the sex of the patient in South Korea from January to May of 2020. 

## Methods 
Deaths from Covid-19 or the results is categorical. 

Sex is categorical. 

# Data Results
## Graphical results    
```{r}
barchartGC(~result + Sex,data=kRdata)
barchartGC(~result + Sex,data=kRdata, type="percent")

```

According to this bar chart, there was a higher percentage of females that survived Covid-19 than men and a higher percentage of men that died from Covid-19 than women. 

## Numerical results
```{r}
table1 <- xtabs(~result + Sex, data=kRdata)
rowPerc(table1)
colPerc(table1)
```

According to this table, there appeared to be higher deaths among men than women. Women have percentages of higher survivial rates concerning Covid-19. 

## Inferential results 
```{r}
chisq.test(table1)
chisqtestGC(table1)
fisher.test(table1)
```

The p-value is 0.001 which is less than 0.05. This means we will reject the null hypothesis and that we conclude that there is a relationship between sex and death from Covid-19 in South Korea from January to May in 2020. 

# Conclusions
